I will keep the farm simple and steady this year. I am 70, my land is only 9 mu, and some people in my family work off-farm, so I will not spread myself too thin with complicated management. Because my main system is wheat-maize and I have well irrigation, I will keep most of the land in that rotation and leave a smaller part for cotton. I will put 6 mu into winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same 6 mu, and 3 mu into cotton. I do this because wheat and maize are the backbone of my farm, they fit my land and water conditions, and I already know how to manage them well. Cotton takes more labor, so I will keep its area smaller.

For seed, I will use better seed rather than old traditional seed, because I want stable emergence and better yield, but I will still manage inputs carefully. For wheat, I will fertilize at a medium level and irrigate a few times because I have wells and wheat responds well to water in key stages. For maize, I will use hybrid seed, give enough nitrogen, and irrigate less than wheat because summer rain helps. For cotton, I will control fertilizer and water more carefully and keep pesticide use higher than the grains, because cotton usually needs more pest attention. On tillage, I will use rotary tillage for wheat and cotton because it is practical for me, and I will use no-tillage for summer maize after wheat to save time and labor. My goal is not to chase the highest possible yield. I want a plan I can finish on time, with lower labor pressure and a stable harvest.
